name: JPMorgan Chase & Co.

reads.name: What they do
reads.evidence: Largest US bank: takes deposits, lends, runs card, markets, investment banking, payments and asset management. Q3 managed revenue $50.9B, net income $15.3B, ROTCE 20%.

reads.name: What they sell
reads.evidence: Q3 net revenue: CCB $21.2B (consumer banking, cards, home lending), CIB $22.7B (banking & payments $11.0B, markets & securities services $11.8B), AWM $6.9B, Corporate $0.1B. Segment ROE: CCB 36%, CIB 18%, AWM 45%.

reads.name: Who buys
reads.evidence: Mass consumer base plus corporates and institutions; no single customer dominates. CCB added 650k+ net new checking accounts; CIB is #1 in global IB fees (9.2% wallet share YTD); AWM AUM $5.2T. Top-customer concentration: nothing found in release.

reads.name: Where they operate
reads.evidence: Mostly US; CIB and AWM are global. Dollar +4.8% over 3m (regime) matters for non-US earnings. Revenue-by-region split not extracted from the 10-K; the legal note lists FX, Russia and India matters. Currency sensitivity not quantified here.

reads.name: Money model
reads.evidence: Spread plus fees plus trading: Q3 NII $27.1B (+13%), noninterest revenue $23.8B (+3%). FY26 NII guide about $106.2B; NII ex-Markets about $97.2B. Fees (card, asset management, IB, payments) offset rate swings. Two-sentence test passes.

reads.name: Operations
reads.evidence: Managed overhead ratio 54% (Q2 47%, Q3'25 52%); expense $27.3B +12% y/y on pay and headcount; FY26 adjusted expense about $108.6B. Banks are people-heavy with high operating leverage to revenue. Guidance hit-rate not measured. Asset-light, no capex burden.

reads.name: Supply chain
reads.evidence: Critical inputs: deposits (avg $2.73T, +8% y/y; #1 US retail deposit share), wholesale funding (LT debt $460B), regulatory capital (CET1 $304B), card rails and technology, and front-office talent (expense +12% from pay and wage inflation). No single supplier; deposit cost is the key chokepoint. Passes rate changes through to loans quickly and to depositors with a lag (signal tags fed_funds, 2y, hy_spreads, regulation, labour). Wage cost pass-through is partial; HY spread widening raises own funding cost and hits IB and markets.

reads.name: Edge
reads.evidence: Scale and breadth: #1 retail deposits for six years, #1 global IB fees, #1 card sales volume; deposits 2.7T and cash/securities $1.5T. Doing differently: building front office (headcount up), retention awards to succession candidates ($20-30M each, June 2026), cut buybacks to $664M net in Q3.

reads.name: Everyday brand
reads.evidence: Chase is a daily-use brand: debit and credit card sales volume +10% y/y, active mobile customers +7%. Customers would notice if it vanished. Marketing spend rose y/y (release); marketing per revenue dollar not extracted.

reads.name: Rivals and share
reads.evidence: Rivals BAC, C, WFC, GS, MS. JPM Q3 revenue +8% y/y against BAC +3%; #1 in IB fees and retail deposits. Share trend inferred from rankings, not a time series.

reads.name: Growth runway
reads.evidence: AWM client net inflows $263B in Q3, AWM loans +20% y/y, payments and securities services double-digit revenue growth, CIB deposits +10%. Already large (NII $106B), so growth is mid single digit to low double digit, mostly priced.

reads.name: Cash and leaders
reads.evidence: ROTCE 20% (21% ex securities loss), YTD 24%; ROTCE FY25 20%; CET1 13.9% vs requirement 11.5% (about $52B above by my calculation: 2.4% x $2.18T RWA). Net payout LTM 61%. Pay: CEO variable pay 88% deferred, 100% PSUs; ROTCE is the company-selected pay measure. FY25 buybacks $31.6B. Bank cash flow is not comparable (operating cash flow -$148B in 2025 from trading balance sheet). Dimon share ownership not extracted.

reads.name: Durability
reads.evidence: Gaining relevance (deposits and AWM inflows growing). Risks: credit cycle (net reserve build $539M, mostly Wholesale), succession (CFO Barnum to hand to de Best after Q1 2027; Co-Presidents Petno and Rohrbaugh named June 2026; Lake retiring), regulation, rate swings. Key-person risk around Dimon is real but being managed.

reads.name: Red flags
reads.evidence: Q3 10-Q: disclosure controls effective, no change in internal control. No 8-K Items 4.01, 4.02, 1.05 or 3.01, no NT filings, no 10-K/A in Nov 2023 to Nov 2026 (my scan of EDGAR submissions). Legal: reasonably possible losses $0 to $1.3B above reserves. SEC comment letters: 3 UPLOAD/CORRESP pairs (2024, 2025, 2026); contents not read. $658M securities loss was labelled discretionary and disclosed.

reads.name: Regime fit
reads.evidence: Overheat: NII up, deposit growth, fees high (+). Slowdown: reserve builds and lower IB and trading, but fees diversify (0 to +). Stagflation: funding cost, credit and securities-loss risk (0 to -). Boom: best case (+). Rate sensitivity: guidance has NII about $28B in Q4. Dollar and input-cost effects small.

reads.name: Rules and politics
reads.evidence: GSIB surcharge 5.5% (effective 2028) would fall to 5.2% if re-proposal is adopted; the Basel III re-proposal alone would raise required CET1 about 6%, both together about 4% (firm estimates). Interchange, FX and Russia litigation open; legal range $0-1.3B. No deal-specific docket pending.

reads.name: Price
reads.evidence: Price $316.74 vs TBV/share $112.64 = 2.81x. At 10% cost of equity and 3% growth that needs a lasting ROTCE of about 22.7% (20.9% at 4% growth). Actual: Q3 20% (21% ex item), 9M26 24% (flattered by a $6.0B Corporate revenue quarter in Q2), FY25 20%. Fair P/TBV at 20.5% is 2.5x ($282, -11%); at 24% it is 3.0x ($338, +7%). P/E 13.3x on TTM EPS $23.85 vs year-end range 9.1x-15.8x (2020-25); year-end 2025 P/TBV 2.94x. Peers: BAC 1.67x, WFC 1.82x, GS 2.35x (sibling files). No cushion.

status_reason: Quality A, but 2.81x tangible book already assumes about 22.7% ROTCE against a 20-21% run rate, so no cushion; no clear market mistake.

stronghold_check.verdict: Confirmed by the numbers. Q3 segment ROE: CCB 36%, CIB 18%, AWM 45%. Streams offset: Q3 CIB net income fell 15% q/q ($8.2B) while AWM stayed $1.8B and CCB revenue rose 9% y/y; NII ex-Markets +6% offsets lower rates; Corporate was -$455M after the securities loss.

findings.fact: Securities loss: $658M pretax ($498M after tax, -$0.18 EPS) net investment securities losses in Treasury and CIO, labelled discretionary and a significant item; ex-item EPS $5.75, ROTCE 21%. Cause beyond 'discretionary' (likely balance-sheet repositioning) not stated in the release text read.
findings.meaning: One-off, not core earnings; EPS vs consensus not verified (analyst numbers excluded).

findings.fact: Q3 EPS $5.57 vs Q2 $7.70: Q2 Corporate net revenue was $6.0B vs $0.1B in Q3; cause of the Q2 item not read.
findings.meaning: Q2 flatters YTD ROTCE (24%), so use 20-21% as run rate.

findings.fact: Reserve build $539M (Q3'25: $810M), mostly Wholesale; net charge-offs $2.2B down $389M; card NCO 2.91%, FY26 card NCO guide about 3.2%.
findings.meaning: Cautious on wholesale credit while consumer credit is fine; matches HY widening.

findings.fact: FY26 NII about $106.2B (YTD $78.2B + Q4 about $28B); adjusted expense about $108.6B; the slides carry a 2027 central-case column (preliminary). Prior-guide change not verified.
findings.meaning: NII near the earlier 'about $106B' view; expense growth (+12% y/y in Q3) is the offset.

findings.fact: CET1 13.9% (Q2 14.2%, Q3'25 14.8%) vs 11.5% requirement; RWA up to $2.18T. Basel re-proposal raises required CET1 about 6%, GSIB re-proposal about 4% net.
findings.meaning: About $52B of excess capital by my calculation; ratio fell as loans grew 10%, so buybacks were cut (Q3 net $664M vs $31.6B in all 2025).

findings.fact: Succession: CFO Barnum to be succeeded by Bregje de Best after Q1 2027 reporting (8-K 2026-11-17); Petno and Rohrbaugh Co-Presidents (June 25, 2026); $20-30M retention awards to four executives; Dimon succession date not disclosed.
findings.meaning: Orderly pipeline, but no CEO date.

feedback.note: JPM Q3 supports the Overheat hard-data read (loans +10% y/y, NII +13%) while the reserve build, lower buyback and CIB revenue -9% q/q fit the market's Slowdown lean; deposits growing 8%.
